components.note: 幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
己 (oneself) — dictionary reads it as a loom with thread; scholars are not sure. Memory aid: a curled-up figure turned in on itself — 'self'. Sound clue in 记 纪 (jì) and 起 (qǐ).
己 (self) — 已 looks like 己 with the gap closed, so do not mix them up. Memory aid: the opening is closed — it is already done (已经).
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom part, as in 布, 帽, 带. 希 is often read as a loosely woven cloth, so 'sparse, rare'; 希望 hope is a later extension.
乂 (crisscross) — Memory aid: crossed threads in an open weave 乂 on cloth 巾 — thin, rare, something you hope for.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
也 (also) — began as a picture (a vessel or snake; scholars disagree) and was borrowed for 'also'. A loose sound clue in 他 tā, 她 tā, 地 dì, 池 chí.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
田 (field) — the bottom part. 备 is simplified from 備; the dictionary story is a trip to the 田 field to prepare for harvest. Treat it as a memory aid.
夂 (going down, slow step) — the top. Memory aid: heading 夂 to the field 田 to get ready — 准备, 设备.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.
⺼ (flesh) — the bottom part, the meat/body radical as in 脑, 脚, 胖. Early forms show meat on a bone, but that does not explain 'willing' today.
止 (stop, foot) — the top. Dictionary story: stop 止 flexing muscle ⺼. Memory aid: you stop resisting and agree — 肯定, a hedged mnemonic.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.
興 (traditional) — several hands lifting together, so to raise, stir, flourish. 兴 keeps only a few strokes; 高兴 is 'high spirits' and 兴趣 is 'interest'.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.
冉 (rǎn) — the main part. The dictionary story is two fish on a line 一: a second catch, so 'again'. It is a memory aid; the origin is unclear.
一 (one) — the top bar. Memory aid: 'one more' line on top — 再见 see you again, 再次 once more.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.
木 (tree) — doubled as 林 on top: a thorny shrub, the original 'bramble'. The wood family appears in 树, 桥. 'Pain' (痛楚) comes from the thorns.
疋 (shū) — the bottom part; the sound clue is only loose today (chǔ vs shū).
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
又 (hand) — the bottom, standing in for the 攴 (tap) of traditional 變. 亦 on top replaces the tangled-thread part and has no meaning link.
變 (traditional) — tangled threads and a tapping hand 攴: sorting out a mess, so 'change'. Read as 'usually explained'.
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
厂 (cliff) — the frame on the left and top, as in 原, 厚, 压. In 厌 it is just the old cliff-like frame of 厭.
犬 (quǎn, dog) — looks like a sound part but quǎn vs yàn is only a loose hint. The old 厭 got its sound from 猒 (yàn).
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
虫 (insect, small creature) — family of 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake. In 虽 it is a leftover of 雖; 'although' has nothing to do with insects.
雖 (traditional) — 虫 plus 唯 (wéi) as sound. 虽 is a simplified shape for it, a grammar word whose parts do not carry its meaning.
勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.
亡 (die, lose) — dictionary: a man in a coffin; early forms may be a person hiding or fleeing. Treat as a memory aid. It also gives sound clues in 忙 máng, 盲 máng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid closed over a person — gone, dead, as in 死亡.
口 (mouth) — the mouth/speech family, as in 吃, 叫, 问. Memory aid: set things apart by calling them out with the mouth — 另外 besides.
力 (strength) — the bottom. No reliable etymology. Memory aid: strength to pull one piece apart from the rest — 'another, separate'.
人 (person) — the top. Common reading: a person standing between two sides, a go-between, as in 介绍 to introduce. Early forms may be armour.
八 (eight, divide) — Dictionary: a border dividing people. Memory aid: a person in the middle of two divided parts — in between.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.
手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).
幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.
厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.
午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
